k1p1-4.name: text#4
k1p1-4.text: $\mathbf{w}\leftarrow\mathbf{w}+\eta\,(y-o)\,\mathbf{x}$  labels $y$ and outputs $o$ are only $+1$ or $-1$

k1p2-2.name: text#2
k1p2-2.text: Two wrong cases merge into one formula

k1p2-19.name: text#19
k1p2-19.text: The 2 is no mystery: $y-o$ is $\pm2$ whenever the signs differ. Chapter 1's $\mathbf{w}\leftarrow\mathbf{w}+\eta y\mathbf{x}$ folds the 2 into the learning rate.

k1p2-21.name: text#21
k1p2-21.text: always add $y\mathbf{x}$: add when the label is $+1$, subtract when $-1$

k1p3-2.name: text#2
k1p3-2.text: Geometry: $\mathbf{w}$ is the boundary's normal vector

k1p3-23.name: text#23
k1p3-23.text:
right: $d\ge0$
wrong: $d<0$
multiplying by the label $y$ avoids the non-differentiable absolute value

k1p4-2.name: text#2
k1p4-2.text: Gradient descent on the wrong points only

k1p4-12.name: text#12
k1p4-12.text:
one wrong point at a time: $\mathbf{w}\leftarrow\mathbf{w}+\eta' y_i\mathbf{x}_i$
differs from the algebraic result only by $\eta'=2\eta$

k1p4-14.name: text#14
k1p4-14.text: algebra and geometry arrive at the same rule

k1p5-2.name: text#2
k1p5-2.text: One update on the wrong point $(0,1)$

k1p5-20.name: text#20
k1p5-20.text: this point is now right: $s$ went from $-0.5$ to $1.5$

k1p6-2.name: text#2
k1p6-2.text: The trajectory matches KP02 step by step

k1p6-21.name: text#21
k1p6-21.text: identical to KP02's binary version, term by term

k1p6-22.name: text#22
k1p6-22.text: the two forms differ only in notation: pass 4 is all right, stop

k1p7-6.name: text#6
k1p7-6.text:
Only wrong points are added.
Add the right ones too and the weights keep growing, possibly pushing right points wrong.

k1p7-8.name: text#8
k1p7-8.text: myth: any value of $\operatorname{sign}(0)$ will do

k1p7-9.name: text#9
k1p7-9.text:
It matters. A point exactly on the boundary falls on the other side and the trajectory changes.
This note takes $+1$.

k1p7-11.name: text#11
k1p7-11.text: update only when wrong; fix the value of $\operatorname{sign}(0)$ first

k1p8-2.name: text#2
k1p8-2.text: A wrong point is pulled to where it belongs

k1p8-7.name: text#7
k1p8-7.text: algebra: four combinations, the two wrong ones merge

k1p8-9.name: text#9
k1p8-9.text: geometry: normal vector and distance, gradient descent on wrong points

k1p8-11.name: text#11
k1p8-11.text: both routes give the same rule

k1p8-13.name: text#13
k1p8-13.text: The Perceptron learns well: can it learn any classification problem? What happens when no straight line separates the two classes?

steps.label: KP03 With ±1 labels the rule shrinks to one line
Four combinations · 1/8
steps.speakerNotes: Write labels and outputs as plus or minus 1. The update formula stays, but y and o have only four combinations.

steps.label: Four combinations · 1/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: y and o equal: error 0, no update. These are the first and last rows.

steps.label: Four combinations · 1/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: y and o differ: the two middle rows are errors. y minus o is plus or minus 2, and both updates reduce to 2 eta y x.

steps.label: Four combinations · 1/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Two kinds of wrong, one formula.

steps.label: One formula · 2/8
steps.speakerNotes: Two ways to be wrong: label plus 1 but guessed minus 1 gives plus 2 eta x; label minus 1 but guessed plus 1 gives minus 2 eta x.

steps.label: One formula · 2/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Both equal 2 eta times y times x, so one formula covers them, applied only when wrong.

steps.label: One formula · 2/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The 2 is no mystery; it is just y minus o being plus or minus 2 when signs differ. Chapter 1's eta y x folds the 2 into the learning rate.

steps.label: One formula · 2/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: A wrong point is pulled toward the side where it belongs.

steps.label: Normal vector and distance · 3/8
steps.speakerNotes: The boundary is the line s equals 0. Subtracting two points on it gives a vector along the boundary; the weight vector w is perpendicular to it, so w is the normal vector, pointing to the firing side.

steps.label: Normal vector and distance · 3/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Signed distances of the four OR points: the origin 1.06; the points 0 1 and 1 0 are minus 0.35, wrong; the point 1 1 is 0.35.

steps.label: Normal vector and distance · 3/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Multiplying the distance by the label gives non-negative for right and negative for wrong, with no non-differentiable absolute value.

steps.label: Normal vector and distance · 3/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: signed distance d=\frac{y\,(\mathbf{w}^\top\mathbf{x}+w_0)}{\|\mathbf{w}\|} right: d\ge0 wrong: d<0 multiplying by the label y avoids the non-differentiable absolute value \mathbf{w}=(1,1), w_0=-1.5: the two wrong points have d=-0.35

steps.label: The geometric route · 4/8
steps.speakerNotes: To fix wrong points, enlarge their d. Over the set of wrong points define the error E, positive when there are mistakes and better when smaller.

steps.label: The geometric route · 4/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Its gradient with respect to w is minus the sum of y x over the wrong points.

steps.label: The geometric route · 4/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Gradient descent gives w plus the learning rate times the sum of y x over the wrong points. One wrong point at a time matches the algebraic result up to the factor 2, folded into the learning rate.

steps.label: The geometric route · 4/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Both routes arrive at the same rule.

steps.label: A numeric check · 5/8
steps.speakerNotes: Take the wrong point 0 1 with label plus 1. Weights 1, 1, bias minus 1.5, so s is minus 0.5 and the output is minus 1: wrong.

steps.label: A numeric check · 5/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Learning rate one half, so 2 eta equals 1 and the update just adds y x: the weights become 1, 2 and the bias minus 0.5.

steps.label: A numeric check · 5/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The new s is 1.5, so this point is now right.

steps.label: A numeric check · 5/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: s rose by 2, exactly 2 eta times the squared length of x plus 1.

steps.label: Same as KP02 · 6/8
steps.speakerNotes: Learn OR again from all zeros, learning rate one half, labels plus or minus 1.

steps.label: Same as KP02 · 6/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The first three updates give 0 0 minus 1, 0 1 0 and 0 1 minus 1.

steps.label: Same as KP02 · 6/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The fourth and fifth updates give 1 1 0 and 1 1 minus 1, and pass four is all right.

steps.label: Same as KP02 · 6/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: These five weights are identical to KP02's binary version; the two forms differ only in notation. The sign function takes plus 1 at 0, consistent with KP01 firing at s at least 0.

steps.label: Same as KP02 · 6/8 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: identical to KP02's binary version, term by term the two forms differ only in notation: pass 4 is all right, stop \operatorname{sign}(0)=+1, matching KP01's fire at s\ge0

steps.label: Two myths · 7/8
steps.speakerNotes: First myth: add y x of every point. No: only wrong points are added; adding the right ones too makes the weights grow forever.

steps.label: Two myths · 7/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Second myth: any value of sign at 0 will do. It matters: a point on the boundary falls on the other side. This note takes plus 1.

steps.label: Two myths · 7/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: myth: any value of \operatorname{sign}(0) will do It matters. A point exactly on the boundary falls on the other side and the trajectory changes. This note takes +1. update only when wrong; fix the value of \operatorname{sign}(0) first

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8
steps.speakerNotes: The point of this unit is one rule: only when wrong, add 2 eta y x to w.

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Algebra and geometry both lead to it.

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: For the next unit: what happens when no straight line separates the two classes?

steps.label: Summary and question · 8/8 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The Perceptron learns well: can it learn any classification problem? What happens when no straight line separates the two classes? next unit: one Perceptron cannot solve XOR
